findings: .dbe/review/diff.patch (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): The change is general. When the leading integral group key is physically clustered (serial IDs, time-ordered data, sorted join output), each interior run gets its own aggregate state and the radix HT is skipped. Nothing in it mentions tables, columns, literals or row counts.

Gates look sufficient. Streaming is disabled for FILTER aggregates, for aggregates with state destructors (ORDER BY/DISTINCT aggregates, varchar min/max, string_agg, list-with-order) and for aggregates without a combine callback. Non-leading group columns may not be float, double or nested. Within a key run they must be constant, checked with DistinctFrom so NULL is handled; otherwise that chunk falls back to ht.AddChunk. Because keys are strictly ordered within a sorted chunk, one key cannot appear in two runs of the same chunk, so each run is one group.

Fallback is correct. If ClusteredIntervalsDisjoint fails (overlap, any_unclustered, external), MergeRunStores inserts every run through a SkipLookups HT that uses the uncombined_data radix bits. It moves the states with CombineStates, then the normal partition combine merges duplicates. The run arenas are kept in stored_allocators, so list segments referenced after combine stay valid. Combine cannot skip the run hand-off, because lstate.ht is always created on the first Sink.

State layout reuse is sound. The fake row pointer (states - aggr_offset) and a stride aligned to 8 let InitializeStates, UpdateStates, FinalizeStates and CombineStates run unchanged. ScanRuns finalizes into the same column positions as Scan (layout.ColumnCount()-1 group columns, hash excluded) and shares the factored Output() mapping.

Minor performance risk, not a correctness issue: if the proof fails late, for example a chunk becomes unclustered after most rows have streamed, MergeRunStores runs serially under the gstate lock in Finalize. Early overlap detection (RegisterRunInterval) limits the common case, and the author measured q03 back to noise. Registering one interval per chunk under a global mutex adds one lock per 2K rows, which is acceptable.
No changes to timing, settings, tests or the shell. The header is untouched and all changes stay within the stated idea.
